PHOTO TILE (1.24.42) -- INDEPENDENT REVIEW 1: FILES AND ARITHMETIC
=====================================================================
Reviewer: a separate agent that did not write the tile. Date: 2026-11-26.
Build tested: the frozen build photo_r1/index.html; its PHOTO_* and GUIDE_PHOTO modules are word for word
src/lantern.inner.html lines 54381-59634 on branch lantern-1.24.42. Note: Lantern.version in that page says "1.24.41".

How to re-run:   python3 run_review.py [path/to/index.html] [--only psd,tiff,export,adjust,filter,blend,select,inpaint] [--json out.json]
Result as found: 455 checks, 37 failed (cases.json holds every row: check, pass, what Lantern gave, what is right).
Run time: about 80 s in Chromium (Playwright), on this cloud machine.

Inputs were made by PIL 12.3, numpy, psd-tools 1.27, ImageMagick 6.9.12 (libtiff 4.5.1), and by hand from Adobe's
Photoshop File Format Specification (review_core.write_psd; psd-tools reads every hand-made file and gives back the
same pixels, which checks the writer). Judges: psd-tools (its reading and its compositor), ImageMagick/libtiff,
PIL, poppler (pdfinfo, pdftoppm), qpdf, SciPy, OpenCV, scikit-image, and textbook formulas written here.
Big pictures (12 MP, 6 MP, 2400 x 1600) are made at run time; inputs/ holds the small ones (1.1 MB).

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FAILURES, MOST IMPORTANT FIRST
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Image > Auto Tone, Auto Contrast and Auto Color do nothing when run from the menu.      [sure: high]
   Input: a dull photo-like picture, values 60..180 (made with numpy). The menu runs
   api.exec(P.ops.adjustCmd("autoContrast"), {}); adjustCmd calls P.adjust.autoContrast(imageData, {}), so the
   params object {} arrives as the "clip" fraction; clipPoints computes n * {} = NaN, finds no cut points and
   returns [0, 255], and Levels 0..255 is no change.
   Lantern gave: range 60..180 after Auto Tone and Auto Contrast (unchanged); Auto Color 48..190 (only its gamma step).
   Right: about 0..255 (called with no second argument, autoContrast does stretch to [0, 255] -- shown in the run).
   Also hit: the ready-made action "Black and white" (its second step is adjust:autoContrast {}), and the Batch.
   Where: PHOTO_ADJ_TONE autoTone/autoContrast/autoColor take (d, clip); PHOTO_OPS adjustCmd passes p.

2. 16-bit Photoshop files saved by Photoshop open without their layers.                    [sure: high]
   Input: inputs/h_16bit_Lr16.psd -- 16-bit RGB, two layers, written per Adobe's spec the way Photoshop writes
   16- and 32-bit documents: the layer info section is empty and the layers are in the "Lr16" tagged block after
   the global layer mask info. psd-tools reads both layers from it.
   Lantern gave: one layer "Background" (the flattened picture) and no note saying layers were dropped.
   Right: layers L64x48 and L16x16, as psd-tools reads them. The same for "Lr32" (h_32bit_zippred_Lr32.psd).
   The same file with the layers in the plain section (h_16bit_plain.psd, as ImageMagick and psd-tools write)
   opens right, so it is only Photoshop's own 16/32-bit files -- the ones scanner and RAW workflows produce.
   Where: PHOTO_PSD_READ read(): nothing after the global layer mask info is read.

3. 16-bit TIFFs with the horizontal predictor (LZW or Deflate) open as noise.               [sure: high]
   Input: im_16_lzw_pred.tif, im_16_zip_pred.tif (RGB) and im_gray16.tif (ImageMagick writes predictor 2 by
   default for 16-bit LZW), made by ImageMagick/libtiff 4.5.1.
   Lantern gave: e.g. pixel (12, 4) [6, 0, 252]; libtiff (ImageMagick) gives [255, 255, 251]; max diff 255.
   Right: the libtiff pixels. Plain and unpredicted 16-bit open right (im_16.tif, im_16_bigendian.tif).
   Where: PHOTO_TIFF read(): "if (pred === 2 && bps === 8)" -- the predictor is undone for 8-bit only. Photoshop
   offers LZW/ZIP with prediction for 16-bit TIFFs, so these are common. Lantern neither refuses nor says.
   Also: 32-bit float with the floating-point predictor (3) opens black (im_float32_zip_pred3.tif). [sure: high]

4. 32-bit PSD layers packed "ZIP with prediction" open wrong.                              [sure: high]
   Input: h_32bit_zippred_plain.psd (one 32-bit float layer, Photoshop's byte-shuffled prediction; psd-tools
   decodes it to the exact floats, max error 3e-8).
   Lantern gave: layer "Float" with max diff 255 from the picture. Raw 32-bit (h_32bit_raw.psd) opens right.
   Where: PHOTO_PSD_READ unpredict() handles depth 8 and 16 only. Photoshop packs 32-bit layers this way.

5. Linear Dodge (Add) is the browser's "lighter", which is not Photoshop's Linear Dodge.   [sure: high]
   Input: random backdrops and sources (sec_blend.py), Lantern.photo.blend.draw.
   With opacity below 100%: backdrop [158, 210, 105] opaque, source [127, 142, 253] at 60%:
     Lantern [234, 255, 255]; Photoshop's rule min(1, b + s) laid on with source-over: [216, 237, 195].
   Over a see-through backdrop: backdrop [86, 237, 16, alpha 128], source [169, 123, 215, alpha 180] at 70%:
     Lantern alpha 254; right alpha 191 (as + ab(1 - as)); colour off by up to 59.
   "lighter" adds premultiplied colour and alpha, so an Add layer at 50% over a bright area clips to white early,
   and two half-clear layers become solid. The other 25 modes agree with W3C / the published Photoshop formulas
   (within the canvas's own rounding) on opaque and see-through pixels, at 100% and below.

6. The flattened picture inside a PSD: Photoshop's convention (colour stored over white) is
   not followed, either way.                                                               [sure: medium-high]
   psd-tools (numpy_io._remove_background / _restore_background, with its fixture evidence) and Photoshop store
   the merged image's colour already composited over white when the document has transparency.
   a) Reading: h_merged_alpha.psd (no layers, merged RGBA, red 200,40,40 stored over white). Lantern gave
      [239, 200, 200, alpha 65]; psd-tools [200, 39, 39, alpha 65]. Affects flat PSDs with transparency only.
   b) Writing: a see-through picture saved by Lantern; psd-tools reads the stored flattened colour at alpha 65 as
      [39, 0, 0] for a picture of [200, 40, 40]. Viewers that show the PSD's flattened picture (Quick Look,
      thumbnails, programs without layer support) will show see-through parts too dark. Layers are not affected.

7. Saving a PSD loses parts of the document that Photoshop keeps.                          [sure: high, by design?]
   a) A layer partly off the canvas is cut to the canvas: pt_layers.psd "Off canvas" bbox (-30,-20,50,40)
      comes back (0,0,50,40). The off-canvas pixels are gone after Open -> Save (Photoshop keeps them).
      Where: PHOTO_FILES save(): each layer is rendered onto a document-sized canvas before it is written.
   b) Groups are not written: h_groups.psd (two groups) opened and saved has 0 groups (layers flattened into the
      list). Neither the help nor the module header says groups are lost on save.
   c) Curves adjustment layers are written with the legacy record only (no "Crv " block). psd-tools logs "Failed to
      read CurvesExtraMarker" and composites the file without the curve (28 levels off). Photoshop's own files
      always carry the "Crv " block; whether Photoshop needs it was not tested (no Photoshop here). [sure: medium]

8. Animated GIF includes hidden layers.                                                     [sure: high]
   PHOTO_FILES' header says "each visible layer a frame of an animation". pt_layers.psd has 8 layers, one hidden:
   Lantern wrote 8 frames (PIL n_frames = 8); right: 7. Where: save(), frames = layers filtered by kind only.

9. Resolution is lost through JPEG and PNG, so "a page of its print size" is wrong for them. [sure: high]
   - A 300-dpi JPEG (photo_small.jpg, JFIF density 300 written by PIL) opens with dpi 72; a 300-dpi PNG (pHYs)
     too. So File > Export PDF / Open as PDF gives a 480 x 360 pt page for a 480 x 360 px, 300-dpi picture
     (right: 115.2 x 86.4 pt). TIFF and PSD resolutions are read right (a 300-dpi TIFF gives 14.64 x 8.88 pt).
   - PNG and JPEG exports carry no resolution (PIL finds no dpi); BMP always says 72 (2835 px/m). Photoshop writes
     pHYs / JFIF density / BMP pixels-per-metre from the document's resolution.

10. Expand and Contract are half a pixel short.                                              [sure: high]
    Input: a 41 x 41 square selection (rows 10..50). Expand 5: rows 5 and 55 are 128 (half chosen), not 255;
    Expand 1: the next row is 128. Contract 5 leaves 33 x 33 with a half-chosen ring (1089 pixels >= 128;
    right: 31 x 31 = 961, as Photoshop's Contract 5 px). Distances are measured centre to centre, so the r-th ring
    sits exactly at t = r and gets 255 * (r + 0.5 - t) = 128. Expanding a single point gives the right disc
    (that convention fits a point but not an edge). Border inherits it.

11. Colours of nearly clear pixels drift.                                                     [sure: high; minor]
    A PNG/TIFF with soft alpha opened and read back: where alpha is 20-63 colours move by up to 6 levels; up to 2
    where alpha >= 64. Cause: layers live in 2D canvases, which hold colour premultiplied by alpha. Alpha itself is
    kept exactly. Photoshop keeps the colours exactly. Worth a line in the help if it stays.

12. Smaller things.
    - Hue/Saturation and Brightness/Contrast disagree with psd-tools' compositor, which is itself reverse-
      engineered from Photoshop files (its own TODOs say "improve accuracy"):                [sure: low-medium]
        * Colorize: Lantern uses Rec.601 luminance for the lightness; psd-tools keeps HSL lightness. Pure yellow
          with hue 200 / sat 60: Lantern [208, 232, 243], psd-tools [51, 153, 204] (142 levels apart on a test
          gradient). I believe Photoshop's Colorize keeps HSL lightness (psd-tools' way), but could not check it.
        * Master hue +40 / sat +30 / lightness -10: up to 27 levels apart (psd-tools applies master lightness
          first, Lantern last).
        * Legacy Brightness/Contrast with negative contrast (-20, -40): Lantern [39, 39, 192], psd-tools
          [30, 30, 183]: psd-tools adds the brightness after the flattening when contrast < 0, Lantern before.
    - Threshold: agrees with psd-tools except at pixels within 1 level of the threshold (weights/rounding).
    - Curves with two points at the same input (128) gives a table of zeros (NaN): only matters if the dialog or
      Chat can make such a pair (not checked).
    - P.adjust.channelMixer({mono: true}) without rows throws a TypeError. The dialog always sets the red row, so
      only Chat/actions calling it directly would hit it.
    - Layer names written without "luni" (psd-tools writes none) are read as Latin-1: "Grüße été" (MacRoman in the
      file) became "Gr\x9f§e \x8et\x8e". Photoshop always writes luni, so this only touches other programs' files.
    - CCITT Group 4 TIFF (bilevel scans, faxes) is refused with a plain message; the module never claimed it.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT IS RIGHT (briefly)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PSD reading: psd-tools' layered file (8 layers: names, order, bounds incl. off-canvas, pixels, opacity, visibility,
blend modes, masks, ZIP and ZIP-predicted 8-bit channels) and ImageMagick's layered file match psd-tools'
composite within 3 levels. Hand-made edge cases right: mask with default colour 255 (outside the mask rectangle
shows), disabled mask, clipping, groups (hidden group hides, half-opaque group), empty layer, layers far off and
half off the canvas, 16-bit with layers in the plain section, 16-bit ZIP+prediction, grayscale, CMYK (plain),
Lab (matches scikit-image's conversion of the stored values), indexed, bitmap, PSB with layers, raw channels,
Unicode names beyond the BMP (emoji) from luni. Adjustment layers levl, curv, brit (+), nvrt, post read with the
right settings and composite as psd-tools does.
PSD writing: psd-tools and ImageMagick read Lantern's files; layer count, names (incl. Unicode), order, opacity,
visibility, blend modes, masks kept; psd-tools' composite of Lantern's file equals Lantern's picture; the stored
flattened picture equals Lantern's picture for an opaque document; Lantern -> PSD -> Lantern is the same picture;
levels/hue2/brit/post/thrs/nvrt written as live adjustment layers psd-tools reads (Levels settings exact).
TIFF reading: none, LZW, LZW+predictor, Deflate (+predictor), PackBits, tiles, planar (strips and tiles), big-endian
(incl. LZW+predictor), 3 rows per strip, 16-bit unpredicted (both byte orders), 32-bit float unpredicted, grey
both ways, 4-bit grey, 1-bit, palette 8 and 4-bit, CMYK, associated and unassociated alpha, grey+alpha, multi-page
(first page and a note), resolution in inches and centimetres, PIL's LZW/Deflate/PackBits/raw, PIL I;16; a
1500 x 1000 noisy LZW+predictor picture is exact. JPEG-packed TIFF is refused with the promised message.
TIFF writing: LZW and plain, RGB and RGBA, read exactly by PIL and libtiff with no warning; a 1500 x 1000 noisy LZW
(many dictionary clears) is exact.
Exports: PNG exact (alpha exact); JPEG quality scale sensible (q12 57.6 dB, q10 41.5 dB, q1 29.4 dB), see-through
flattened on white or on the chosen colour; WebP keeps alpha; BMP V4 32-bit read exactly with alpha by PIL and
ImageMagick; GIF of a 40-colour picture with rare colours is exact, a photo at 256 colours is fine, transparency
under half solid is clear, ImageMagick reads it cleanly; animated GIF delay and loop right; PDF passes qpdf and
poppler renders the picture.
Adjustments (formula checks): neutral settings are identities; Levels (incl. channel then master, in = out step);
Curves = SciPy natural spline, through its points, flat beyond; Posterize; Threshold; Invert; Desaturate (HSL);
Equalize = OpenCV equalizeHist; legacy Brightness/Contrast (+); Exposure in linear light with offset and gamma;
Channel Mixer; Gradient Map; Black & White defaults (pure colours give 40/60/40/60/20/80 % of 255, greys stay);
Hue/Sat hue +120, saturation -100 = HSL lightness, reds range, lightness +-100; Vibrance favours dull colours;
Photo Filter keeps luminosity; Auto Color (called directly) neutralises a cast; greys stay grey and alpha is
untouched in every one tried; extremes (exposure +20, contrast 100, gamma 0) give no garbage.
Filters: Gaussian = SciPy gaussian_filter (nearest edges) at radius 0.3-20 on 203 x 151 within 1 level; the
six-box path within 0.5-1.8 levels (2400 x 1600 r10 in 2.7 s, 3000 x 4000 r2 in 3.0 s, 1000 x 800 r60), well
inside its claim of 4; 1 x 1, 1 x 57, 57 x 1, 2 x 3 fine; no dark fringe on a red disc on clear (Gaussian, box,
motion, resize). Box = uniform_filter; Median, Minimum, Maximum exactly = SciPy; Unsharp and High Pass = the
formulas; flat colour stays flat under 12 filters (edges included); motion blur runs along its angle; Add Noise
uniform statistics, mono, repeatable. Resize: Lantern equals a textbook separable resampler (independent float
code) within 1 level for bilinear, bicubic (a = -0.5) and Lanczos 3, up and down; PIL differs at a handful of
pixels (it rounds and clips between passes; mean 0.2); Mitchell = ImageMagick's within 2; nearest exact; 300 x 1 ok.
Rotate 90/-90/180 exact; 30 degrees grows the canvas right and matches PIL's bicubic (mean <= 3). Homography =
OpenCV getPerspectiveTransform; perspective warp = OpenCV warpPerspective (bilinear) once the half-pixel
convention is matched.
Blending: 25 of 27 modes right (see 5); Dissolve takes ~30% at 30%, none blended.
Selections: wand tolerance inclusive (100 +32 in, +33 out), contiguous and not, tolerance 0; colour range
fuzziness rule exact; feather = Gaussian sigma r; border, smooth, grow, similar behave; Layer Via Copy of a
feathered selection: alpha = selection, colours kept, picture unchanged; a filter inside a feathered selection is
old + (new - old) x selection.
Content-Aware Fill / healing: a pole across sky and grass is removed, sky filled with sky and grass with grass,
every pixel outside the hole unchanged; 12 MP picture: 24 x 24 hole in 0.6 s, 600 x 400 hole in 13.6 s, nothing
outside the selection changed, the dark block gone. Healing a patch 50 levels darker onto a gradient takes the
gradient's light (mean error <= 2) and leaves the outside alone.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NOT TESTED / COULD NOT TEST
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Photoshop itself (not available): every "as Photoshop does" is judged by Adobe's specification, psd-tools,
  ImageMagick and published formulas. Whether Photoshop accepts Lantern's PSD (no blending ranges written, legacy-
  only curves, 8-byte brit block) is untested; GIMP, Krita and Photopea were not available either.
- pytoshop was not tried (psd-tools 1.27 plus hand-made bytes covered the cases).
- Duotone and multichannel PSDs, vector masks with a user mask ("real" mask rectangle, channel -3), layer masks
  with the "relative to layer" flag, mask parameters (flag bit 4), PSB above 4 GB.
- TIFF: 2-bit, 16-bit palette, 32-bit integer, YCbCr, old-style JPEG, BigTIFF (refused by design), orientation
  tag, FillOrder 2, files over a few MB of LZW (the decoder builds arrays per code; speed on a 100 MB TIFF untested).
- Phone photos with Exif orientation (the browser decoder handles it; not checked), HEIC/AVIF, SVG.
- The UI dialogs themselves (Curves point dragging, Levels boxes) -- only the commands they call.
- Distort filters (twirl, pinch, spherize, polar, wave, zigzag, lens), Stylize beyond emboss/find edges on flat
  colour, Pixelate, Render: no public definition to hold them to; only flat-colour sanity was checked for a few.
- Add Noise Gaussian: Lantern's std is amount/2 (12.7 for 10%); Photoshop's definition is not published.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
